summary: Editor preview no longer renders 'Preview error: <eof> expected' banners or blinks black during Claude script generation. Partial Lua scripts are now syntactically validated before they reach MoonSharp; truncated chunks are auto-completed when possible and silently dropped when not, leaving the previously rendered scene intact.

rootCause.explanation: RunPartialScript handed every streamed chunk straight to LuauGameRunner.RunGamePreview, which calls TearDown() before parsing. When a chunk arrived truncated mid-block (function/if/for), MoonSharp threw 'end' expected near '<eof>' AFTER the previous scene had already been destroyed. The catch in LuauGameRunner.RunScript (Assets/Scripts/LuauGameRunner.cs:565-579 pre-fix) then wrote 'Preview error: ...' to the _editorError React global, causing both the red banner and the black scene the user reported.

additions: public static bool IsStreamingPartialScript — gates parse-error notifications and TearDown side-effects
LuaBlockBalance / IsLuaScriptComplete — count opener vs closer keywords AFTER stripping strings + comments
AutoCompleteLuaScript — appends N missing 'end' statements when balance > 0
TryParseLua — dry-run MoonSharp LoadString to confirm grammar before RunScript ever touches the scene
StripLuaStringsAndComments — handles short strings, long strings ([[...]] and [=[...]=]), line comments, block comments
modifications: RunScript catches (ScriptRuntimeException + Exception) now suppress _editorError when IsStreamingPartialScript is true; same for the unfilled-placeholder and 30s-timeout branches
RunPartialScript now sanitizes the chunk, runs IsLuaScriptComplete, attempts AutoCompleteLuaScript + TryParseLua, and drops the partial entirely (no TearDown) if both checks fail
StartBuildPreview sets IsStreamingPartialScript = true and calls ClearEditorError() to clear any stale banner
LaunchAsync editMode branch + RunGame play path + ExitAsync clear IsStreamingPartialScript so genuine post-build errors still surface
Added private ClearEditorError() helper that wipes _editorError on every ReactRendererUGUI
_editorError poller now skips parse-style errors (regex on 'Preview error|Script error|<eof>|end expected|...') while isBuilding is true, and wipes the global so it can't latch in afterward
Added a useEffect that clears previewError + Globals._editorError on the rising edge of isBuilding
Banner JSX guarded with !isBuilding for defense-in-depth

validation.method: Ran LuauGameRunner.LuaBlockBalance / IsLuaScriptComplete / AutoCompleteLuaScript / TryParseLua against 7 hand-crafted partials via Unity's script-execute MCP after AssetDatabase refresh.

results.input:
Scene.SetSkybox("day")
local function spawnEnemy(x, z)
  local e = Object.Create("cube")
  e:SetPosition(x, 1, z)
results.autoCompleted:
Scene.SetSkybox("day")
local function spawnEnemy(x, z)
  local e = Object.Create("cube")
  e:SetPosition(x, 1, z)
end
results.behavior: RECOVERED — partial executes, scene materializes incrementally

results.case: nested function+if with mid-call truncation (unclosed paren)
results.input: Game.OnStart(function()\n  if Player.GetHealth() < 30 then\n    UI.Show("Low HP")
results.behavior: DROPPED — can't repair an unclosed paren by appending end; previous scene survives, no banner, no black blink

results.input: for i = 1, 10 do\n  local b = Object.Create("cube")\n  b:SetPosition(i, 0, 0)

results.case: opener keywords inside a short string
results.input: print("function for if while end")\nlocal x = 1
results.behavior: PASS-THROUGH — string contents correctly ignored by counter

results.input:
local s = [[
function foo() if x then
]]
print(s)

results.case: opener keyword in a line comment

errorBannerSuppressionScope: Suppression is gated on LuauGameRunner.IsStreamingPartialScript (C#) and isBuilding (React). Both flip off the moment LaunchAsync(editMode:true) calls runner.RunGamePreview with the full validated script — at which point genuine parse/runtime errors in a published script surface to the banner exactly as before. ExitAsync also clears the C# flag as a safety net. So error suppression applies only during streaming.

templateGameRegressionTests.reason: End-to-end verification of all 7 template games requires kicking off live Claude generation jobs through the actual Pludo API + Anthropic key. Static validator cases above prove the parsing logic; a follow-up live run with each template should confirm zero red banners + zero black blinks across the full streaming window.
manualSteps: Open the Create tab, generate each of the 7 templates (Platformer, Racer, Shooter, Puzzle, Sandbox, RPG, Tower Defense)
Watch Unity console for [GameLauncher] Auto-completed truncated partial script. and [GameLauncher] Partial unrecoverable — keeping prior scene. log lines
Confirm no red 'Preview error' banner appears at any point before status flips to script_ready
Confirm scene never goes solid black between partials
After done state, deliberately edit the published script to be invalid via the chat (e.g. ask AI to break it) and confirm the banner DOES appear — proving suppression is streaming-scoped only

knownLimitations: Standalone do ... end blocks aren't tracked as openers (rare in AI-generated code; falls through dry-run check)
repeat ... until depth is counted but auto-complete only appends 'end', so a truncated repeat block still fails the dry-run and is dropped (correct — silently skipped)
Auto-complete only repairs missing 'end's; truncated expressions (unclosed parens, dangling operators) are dropped to keep the prior scene
